Purpose-built for coding agents. Built-in stateful adapters, scoped security boundaries, transactional DAG rollbacks, and real-time MCP verification.

Stateful Database Adapters

Provision PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, and SQLite with automated volume retention, staged credential isolation, and health verification.

adapter // postgres:16 active_lease
volume_mount: /var/lib/smoooth/volumes/pgdata
health_probe: pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres (12ms)
credential_scope: staged_rotation [dual_auth: active]
retention_policy: snapshot_before_destroy (safety_lock: ON)
Database container isolated on private bridge network

Scoped Security & Least Privilege

Never grant an AI agent an unrestricted root shell. Enforce 256-bit cryptographic bearer tokens with granular role permissions (read_only, plan, deploy, admin).

auth // token_guard sha256_hashed
token_id: smoooth_sec_9f82c4... [256-bit]
granted_scopes: ["read_only", "plan", "deploy"]
prohibited: ["host_root_shell", "arbitrary_write"]
sandboxing: systemd (NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict)
bind_address: 127.0.0.1:4040 (loopback private)
Agent confined to scoped workspace boundaries

Transactional 2-Phase DAG Deployments

Every deployment validates an execution plan before provisioning. If a container fails health checks, Smoooth rolls back automatically to the last healthy state.

dag // 2-phase_pipeline rollback_ready
01 PLAN → create_plan(web_app:v1.2, postgres:16)
• Canonical hash: sha256:7f8a92e104cd...
02 PROVISION → execute_plan(fencing_lease: acquired)
• Health probes: HTTP /healthz [200 OK, 14ms]
• Safe promotion: Caddy reverse proxy updated
Checkpoint committed. Zero downtime release active.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) Stream

Inspect topological DAG steps, container log streams, and environment health probes directly from your agent conversation or terminal.

audit // mcp_stream append_only
[14:32:01] mcp:call → scan_foreign_workloads()
→ 3 running Docker containers adopted into workspace
[14:32:03] mcp:call → create_service_binding(app, db)
→ Staged credentials injected into container env
[14:32:04] mcp:call → configure_ingress(domain: "api.site.dev")
→ Automatic ACME TLS certificate issued
Signed audit entry recorded at /var/lib/smoooth/audit.jsonl

From VPS to Agent-Operated

1. Install Daemon

Run the idempotent installer on Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12. Sets up sandboxed systemd daemon and Docker bridge.

$ curl -fsSL https://smoooth.dev/install.sh | bash

2. Pair Coding Agent

Pair Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf directly over local loopback using your 256-bit scoped bearer token.

$ claude mcp add --transport sse smoooth http://127.0.0.1:4040/sse

Scenario // Solo SaaS & Indie Founders

Eliminate OOM build crashes on $5/mo VPS nodes

Coolify consumes 1.4 GB RAM just idling with PHP, Laravel Horizon, and internal daemons. When Next.js builds trigger on a 2 GB VPS, the Linux kernel terminates your Postgres database.

1.35 GB RAM Reclaimed: Smoooth idles at under 28 MB.
Volume Lock: Automatic pgdata retention prevents data loss.
Zero-Downtime TLS: Embedded Caddy with sub-second ACME.

Technical Guarantees
& FAQ.

Clear answers on compatibility, security boundaries, container orchestration, and real-world limitations.

How do AI coding agents like Claude Code or Cursor interact with Smoooth?
Smoooth implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard. AI agents pair over stdio (spawning smoooth mcp) or streamable HTTP/SSE (http://127.0.0.1:4040/sse) using a 256-bit bearer token. Instead of running unsafe shell scripts as root, agents invoke structured, typed tools like create_plan, execute_plan, verify_connection, and configure_ingress.
Is giving an AI coding agent Docker daemon access secure?
Smoooth isolates all agent execution through four layers of defense: (1) Loopback binding to 127.0.0.1:4040 with zero public port exposure; (2) Role-based bearer token scopes (read_only, plan, deploy, admin); (3) Systemd sandboxing (NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict); and (4) Append-only signed audit logging of every container operation.
What databases and Linux distributions are supported?
Smoooth is verified on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Debian 12 (x86_64 and ARM64). It provides native stateful adapters for PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, and SQLite with automated persistent volume management, credential rotation, and container health probes.
How does Smoooth compare to Coolify or Dokku?
Coolify requires 2 CPUs and 2 GB RAM minimum, running a full web dashboard, Fastify backend, and Traefik proxy. Smoooth is a single static Rust binary consuming under 28MB RAM idle, purpose-built for autonomous AI agents over MCP with transactional 2-phase DAG deployments and automatic rollbacks if health probes fail. See our Smoooth vs Coolify comparison or our Claude Code deployment guide.
Can I run Smoooth on a low-cost $5/mo VPS or homelab?
Yes. Minimum requirements are 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, and 10 GB disk space. Because Smoooth is compiled in Rust with zero background Node.js/PHP runtime overhead, your VPS resources remain 100% dedicated to your actual application workloads.
